instruction: Write JavaScript code that demonstrates the difference between var, let and const inside a for loop, printing the captured values after the loop ends.
Write a JavaScript function makeCounter that returns an increment function using a closure so each counter keeps its own private count.
Write JavaScript code using an IIFE to create a module-scoped private variable that cannot be read from outside.

Write JavaScript code that demonstrates function hoisting versus variable hoisting: call a function declaration before its line, and show what happens when reading a let variable before initialization.
Write JavaScript code that fixes the classic loop-callback problem so each callback logs its own iteration index, using let instead of var.
Write a JavaScript once(fn) utility that uses a closure so fn is invoked at most one time, returning undefined on later calls.
Write a JavaScript curry(fn) function that converts a 3-argument function into a curried version using closures.
Write JavaScript code that creates a bank account with deposit/withdraw private state via a closure, throwing on overdraft.
Write JavaScript code that shows block scoping: declare let x inside an if block and try to access it outside.
Write a JavaScript createMultiplier(multiplier) closure that returns a function multiplying its argument by the captured factor.
Write JavaScript code demonstrating that primitives are copied by value while objects are shared by reference when assigned between variables.
Write JavaScript code showing that const prevents rebinding but not mutation of object contents, then freezing the object to make it immutable.
Write JavaScript code where a closure captures a variable from an outer function and the captured value survives after the outer function returns.

Write a JavaScript makeBank() that returns methods shareBank(sibling) style privileged access: two account objects created inside one closure that can inspect each other's balances only through a provided method.
Write a JavaScript memoize(fn) that caches results per-argument using a closure and a Map.
Write JavaScript code that demonstrates accidental global variables in sloppy mode and how "use strict" turns the same assignment into a ReferenceError.
Write JavaScript code that shadows an outer let variable with a block-scoped one and logs both values from their respective scopes.
Write a JavaScript adder() closure factory where the returned function accumulates its running total across calls.
Write JavaScript code where each call to makeLabeler(prefix) produces an independent closure that prefixes its argument, and prove the two labelers do not share state.
